items.summary: 8pm Alex Harding & Lucian Ban - "DARK BLUE" Toronto Release Concert
items.description:
Detroit-born baritone saxophonist Alex Harding and Transylvanian expat, New York City–based pianist Lucian Ban are longtime collaborators and leading voices in contemporary jazz. Over more than two decades, they have founded multiple projects together, released acclaimed recordings on American and European labels, and performed extensively across the U.S. and Europe.

DARK BLUE (Sunnyside Records) is a celebration of their musical brotherhood—a duo exploration blending original compositions and improvisations shaped by jazz, blues, and European chamber music. From avant-blues and spontaneous improvisations to lyrical ballads and Sun Ra–inspired atmospheres (Harding is a frequent collaborator with the Arkestra), DARK BLUE captures two master musicians in deep, intuitive dialogue.

As legendary tuba player Howard Johnson writes in the album’s liner notes:
“Lucian and Alex have been honing their duo craft for some years. Now they have become one voice when they want to and still manage to complement each other.”

Lucian Ban – Piano

Alex Harding – Baritone Saxophone & Percussion

items.description:
Chicago/Detroit based ensemble "Teiku" reframes unique and rare Eastern European ancestral passover melodies in an improvised music setting. The expansive possibilities of instant composition, the ritualistic origins of the melodies, and the inspiration of jazz pioneers like Ornette Coleman and Muhal Richard Abrams all contribute to the immersive world of Teiku.

The band features bass clarinetist Jason Stein (Natural Information Society, Hearts and Minds), bassist Jaribu Shahid (Art Ensemble of Chicago, Sun Ra Arkestra, Geri Allen), and founders pianist Josh Harlow (Vincent Davis, Wadada Leo Smith) and percussionist Jonathan Barahal (saajtak, Wadada Leo Smith, Michael Formanek). Teiku is releasing their sophomore album, Klang, this June on Ginkgo Records.

This July, join an intimate five-part jazz series spotlighting acclaimed Cape Town–born trumpeter Muneeb Hermans, whose sound blends soulful tradition with world-class experience. Each evening offers a distinct musical journey—from cinematic storytelling and jazz standards to original compositions and bold collaborations—set in an atmosphere designed for close listening and connection.

The series opens on July 5th with Muneeb Herman's Quartet, followed by July 11th showcasing his Quintet interpreting beloved jazz standards. On July 18th, the Quintet returns with music from Muneeb’s acclaimed album One for HP, before the season culminates in a special finale on July 25th featuring an expanded lineup and surprise guest appearances, bringing the series to an unforgettable close. On July 26th his quartet is returning to CONTXT for a special Wrap-up concert.

Afro Brasilica is a multidisciplinary creative residency that champions sound, movement and conversation. Rooted in music, including but not limited to: Brazilian Samba, Afro-Latin, Latin Jazz and more, the project expands on the idea of community cultivation through shared expression within CONTXT. 

Through dynamic DJ sets, visual art, poetry, dialogue, guest performances, spirited libations and curated tapas, Afro Brasilica weaves a limitless, intentional approach like the rings of its latter-namesake wood; intricate and unique, yet, connected and intersectional.

items.description:
4 Weeks, 4 Bands, 4 Horns... For Sonny Rollins

One of the greatest Jazz Saxophonist of all time, WALTER THEODORE "SONNY" ROLLINS was born on September 7, 1930 in New York City. He grew up in Harlem not far from the Savoy Ballroom, the Apollo Theatre, and the doorstep of his idol, Coleman Hawkins. After early discovery of Fats Waller and Louis Armstrong, he started out on alto saxophone, inspired by Louis Jordan. At the age of sixteen, he switched to tenor, trying to emulate Hawkins. He also fell under the spell of the musical revolution that surrounded him, bebop.He began to follow Charlie Parker, and soon came under the wing of Thelonious Monk, who became his musical mentor and guru. When he was living in Sugar Hill, his neighborhood musical peers included Jackie McLean, Kenny Drew, and Art Taylor, but it was young Sonny who was first out of the pack, working and recording with Babs Gonzales, J.J. Johnson, Bud Powell, and Miles Davis before he turned twenty.
